components.gap: The full treatment promised by proved=annex:p15.model-density-invariance lacks any argument or worked boundary for the theorem's stated negative coordinate claim (body 136-137: 'Declaring a new flat prior in the new coordinates is not such a transport in general'). The declared annex item proves only the transported case (annex 97-102). It then restates the negative claim (annex 103-104) without a counterexample or derivation. The worked example after the theorem (body 148-155) concerns density versions at a null point, not parameter coordinates. A suitable instance exists in thm:p15-bayes-transformation (parts/p15/bayesian-updating-prediction.tex 313-319; annex 372-392), but this theorem and its proof never cite it. Every other element of C003 is present at the cited lines: the version change, the intrinsic Q_* comparison via RN uniqueness, d nu' = h d nu, parameter transport, the observation bijection and the null-point example.

defect_observations.observation: The negative claim 'Declaring a new flat prior in the new coordinates is not such a transport in general' sits inside a proved theorem but has no proof. The declared annex item (annex 97-104) proves only the transported case and restates the negative claim. No coordinate example appears in this chapter. The applicable instance in thm:p15-bayes-transformation (parts/p15/bayesian-updating-prediction.tex 313-319) is not cited. A citation or a short in-chapter instance would close the gap.

The notation clashes with the source. In KR95 eq. (16) (p. 784, PDF p. 13; text lines 813-840), alpha_k is the prior odds pr(H_k)/pr(H_0) with alpha_0 = B_00 = 1. The handbook uses alpha_k for prior probabilities that sum to one and does not mention the difference. This is not counted as a component failure: the body cites only eqs. (17)-(19) at line 344 and never reproduces eq. (16).

Three one-step consequences of definitions are not written out (not counted as gaps). C002: 'a prior-zero model has posterior probability zero on G'; annex 39-41 says only 'including zero model prior weights', and the result follows from w_k = alpha_k m_k / e with m_k finite on G. C003: annex 84-85 asserts that {sum alpha_k r_k > 0} has full Q_alpha-mass without the one-line computation. C009: annex 289-290 gives only the 'positive if means differ' direction; the 'otherwise unchanged' direction follows from a_k = a.

KR95 Sec 5.1 (p. 781, PDF p. 10; text lines 636-647) objects to the conditional prescription pi(beta|H0) = pi(beta|psi=psi0,H1) because it depends on the parameterization (Jacobian; Borel paradox, Savage/Dickey). The handbook instead demonstrates version non-uniqueness on a null set (body 391-396, 408-414) and never states the parameterization dependence. Its attributions at body 200 and 414 remain consistent with the source. This is not counted against C004 or C011, because their entry texts do not claim the parameterization point.
